title: Continuation findings must LEAD with 'repair or retract these RED artifacts first' — retries build new work while the prior attempt's broken test sits untouched
summary: Cycles 1492 and 1495 (verdict-cache retries) each produced all-green NEW predicates while the inherited cycle-1488 unsatisfiable predicate — the sole red, whose correct one-line fix was even written in a sibling predicate's COMMENT — went untouched through two full retries. The findings injection (continuation_stamp.go readContinuationFindings) serves the prior audit-fail-reason as context, but nothing instructs the builder to prioritize repairing/retracting the failing artifacts before new work.
root_cause: The findings block is descriptive, not prescriptive: it reports why the prior attempt failed but does not order the retry's first action. Builders optimize for the item's acceptance criteria and treat prior-cycle test files as not-theirs-to-touch.
fix: (1) In the continuation findings rendering (core/continuation_stamp.go readContinuationFindings / the build prompt injection seam), when the prior failure includes EGPS red predicates or named failing artifacts, PREPEND a mandatory header: 'FIRST ACTION: the following artifacts are RED on your base — repair or retract each BEFORE any new work: <paths+one-line reasons>'. (2) Builder persona: prior-cycle ACS predicate files in the lane's own go/acs/cycle*/ ARE yours to repair on a continuation. Deterministic Go for (1), persona line for (2). Red-first: fixture continuation with a red inherited predicate — the rendered findings block must lead with the repair directive naming the file.
acceptance: Findings block on a red-predicate continuation leads with the FIRST-ACTION repair directive naming exact files — red-first fixture.
No change when the prior failure carries no named red artifacts (descriptive block unchanged).
